title: Trying · if it is · frequency
titleJp: たこやきなら、食べてみたい！
canDo: I can say I'll try doing something and invite someone to try it, with 〜てみる: 食べてみてください, 着てみてもいいですか.
I can say what I'd like to try (〜てみたい) and tell what I tried (〜てみました), without mixing it up with 〜たことがある.
I can respond to a topic the other person brought up with noun + なら ("if it's X…"), to recommend something or to make a contrast: 日曜日ならひまです.
I can say and ask how often I do something: 一週間に三回, 一日に一時間, 一か月に何回…？

blocks.t: Warm-up: say out loud the て-form of 10 verbs (lesson 06-1), including する, 来る and 行く
Vocabulary: tap 🔊 on each word and repeat it twice; count aloud from 一回 to 十回
Grammar: the 3 points, each with its examples read aloud and one 🔬
Video (block 6), only the part on なら
Notebook homework + checking it against the answer key
Checklist (block 10) + write your questions in the lesson notebook

skills: The て-form of every verb (lesson 06-1). 〜てみる is built straight from it.
〜てください (lesson 06-2), 〜てもいいですか (lesson 06-3) and 〜たい (lesson 11-1): 〜てみる combines with all three.
〜たことがある (lesson 11-2), so that you don't mix up "I have done it before" with "I tried it".
Contrastive は (lesson 03-2), frequency words such as よく and ときどき (lesson 03-3) and 〜時間 (lesson 04-3).
The potential from lesson 13-1 (会える, 行ける, ひける), which appears in the answers with なら.

vocab.en: to do something and see how it is; to try doing
than I thought, than I expected
curry (the Japanese kind is a thick stew served with rice)
very fond of, love (〜が大好きです = I love…)
… time(s) (一回 = いっかい, once)
one day (a length of time; ついたち is "the first" of the month)
medicine (くすりを飲む = to take medicine)
food stall (at a festival or on the street)
takoyaki, balls of batter with a piece of octopus inside

grammar.title: 〜てみる: trying something out
grammar.gloss: do something and see how it is
grammar.explanation:
〜てみる means **doing something to see what it's like**: trying it, tasting it, testing it. It is the verb's **て-form** + **みる**. みる is the same verb "to see", in the sense of "do it and see how it goes". As a helper verb, it is usually written **in kana**: 食べてみる.
• **Form**: て-form (lesson 06-1) + みる. 食べる → 食べてみる; 行く → 行ってみる; 着る → 着てみる; する → してみる. Even 見る works: 見てみる = have a look and see.
• **みる does the conjugating**, like a る-verb: 食べてみます, 食べてみました (I tried it), 食べてみたい (I want to try it), 食べてみてください (try it!), 食べてみましょう (let's try it).
• The most useful combinations in daily life: **〜てみたいです** for wishes (いつか着物を着てみたいです), **〜てみてください** for recommending, and **〜てみてもいいですか** for asking to try something on or test it in a shop.
• 〜てみる means you **really do it**, to find out the result. English "try" is broader: when it means an effort you keep up as a habit ("I try to get up early every day"), Japanese usually uses another form, 〜ようにする, which comes in lesson P-01.
• **〜てみる × 〜たことがある**: 食べてみました tells about one action, one time ("I tried it"). 食べたことがあります (lesson 11-2) says you have that experience in your life ("I have eaten it before").
• In the sentence, [verb in て + みる] is a single block, the **PREDICATE**. The thing you try keeps **を**: カレーを作ってみました.
grammar.structure: [verb in て] + みる · 〜てみたいです · 〜てみてください · 〜てみてもいいですか

examples.jp: これはブラジルのパン・デ・ケージョです。食べてみてください。
examples.kana: これはブラジルのパン・デ・ケージョです。たべてみてください。
examples.romaji: Kore wa Burajiru no pan de kējo desu. Tabete mite kudasai.
examples.en: This is Brazilian cheese bread. Please try some!

examples.jp: このシャツ、着てみてもいいですか。— はい、どうぞ。
examples.kana: このシャツ、きてみてもいいですか。— はい、どうぞ。
examples.romaji: Kono shatsu, kite mite mo ii desu ka. — Hai, dōzo.
examples.en: May I try on this shirt? — Yes, go ahead.

examples.jp: きのう、はじめて日本のカレーを作ってみました。思ったより、かんたんでした。
examples.kana: きのう、はじめてにほんのカレーをつくってみました。おもったより、かんたんでした。
examples.romaji: Kinō, hajimete Nihon no karē o tsukutte mimashita. Omotta yori, kantan deshita.
examples.en: Yesterday I tried making Japanese curry for the first time. It was easier than I thought.

pitfalls: Before みる comes the て-form: 食べみる ✗ / 食べるみる ✗ → 食べてみる ✓. Careful with う-verbs: 行きてみる ✗ → 行ってみる ✓.
みる, at the end, does the conjugating: 食べてみるたい ✗ → 食べてみたい ✓; 食べたいてみる ✗.
For "have you ever tried it?", the natural choice is the experience form: 食べたことがありますか ✓ (lesson 11-2). 食べてみましたか asks about one specific occasion ("did you try the one I gave you?").
howToStudy: Write 6 verbs in your notebook in three forms: 〜てみたいです, 〜てみました and 〜てみてください (食べてみたいです / 食べてみました / 食べてみてください…). Read them aloud, checking the て-form of each one.

Tap 🔬 on example 3. 作ってみました shows up as a single block, the PREDICATE; カレーを is the OBJECT (with 日本の as DESCRIBES NEXT); きのう is TIME and はじめて is HOW / HOW OFTEN. Read it backwards: tried making → what? → Japanese curry → when? → yesterday, for the first time.
Make a list of 5 things you want to try in Japan and say each one out loud with 〜てみたいです: 着物を着てみたいです。おんせんに入ってみたいです。…

grammar.title: N なら: "if it's X…"
grammar.gloss: picking up a topic and saying what applies to it
grammar.explanation:
**なら** takes a topic that **has already come up** in the conversation, almost always brought up by the other person, and says something that applies **specifically** to it: "if it's X…", "if you mean X…", "as for X, then…".
• **Form**: noun + なら, **without だ**. 日曜日なら; ブラジル料理なら.
• **Use 1 · recommending or informing**: someone mentions a topic, and you give a tip about it. ブラジル料理が食べたいんですが。— ブラジル料理なら、駅の前の店がいいですよ。
• **Use 2 · contrast, "that one, yes"**: you set one item apart from the others. 土曜日はアルバイトがありますが、日曜日ならひまですよ。 (Saturday no, Sunday yes). The other half often comes with contrastive は (lesson 03-2).
• **Use 3 · from the group to one item**: the question is broad, and the answer picks out one part. スポーツは好きですか。— サッカーなら大好きです。 (sports in general, not so much; soccer, yes).
• That is why なら almost never starts a conversation out of nowhere: it **responds** to something that is already on the table.
• You will also hear なら after verbs (行くなら…, "if you're going…"). In this lesson, stick to noun + なら.
• In the sentence, the block with なら is the **condition** (🔬 labels it IF / WHEN), and the comment about X comes after it, ending in the **PREDICATE**. Read from the end: "I'm free" → when? → if it's Sunday.
grammar.structure: [N] なら、[what applies to N]。 (no だ: 日曜日なら)

examples.jp: しゅうまつ、ひまですか。— 土曜日はアルバイトがありますが、日曜日ならひまですよ。
examples.kana: しゅうまつ、ひまですか。— どようびはアルバイトがありますが、にちようびならひまですよ。
examples.romaji: Shūmatsu, hima desu ka. — Doyōbi wa arubaito ga arimasu ga, nichiyōbi nara hima desu yo.
examples.en: Are you free this weekend? — I have my part-time job on Saturday, but on Sunday I'm free.

examples.jp: ブラジル料理が食べたいんですが。— ブラジル料理なら、駅の前の店がいいですよ。
examples.kana: ブラジルりょうりがたべたいんですが。— ブラジルりょうりなら、えきのまえのみせがいいですよ。
examples.romaji: Burajiru ryōri ga tabetai n desu ga. — Burajiru ryōri nara, eki no mae no mise ga ii desu yo.
examples.en: I'd like to eat Brazilian food… — If it's Brazilian food, the restaurant in front of the station is good.

examples.jp: ルーカスさん、スポーツは好きですか。— サッカーなら大好きです。
examples.kana: ルーカスさん、スポーツはすきですか。— サッカーならだいすきです。
examples.romaji: Rūkasu-san, supōtsu wa suki desu ka. — Sakkā nara daisuki desu.
examples.en: Lucas, do you like sports? — If it's soccer, I love it.

pitfalls: No だ before なら: 日曜日だなら ✗ → 日曜日なら ✓.
なら responds to a topic that has already come up. Walking up out of nowhere and saying ラーメンなら、あの店がいいですよ sounds strange: first someone mentions ramen, then comes なら.

は only marks the topic; なら adds "if it's this one (and not another)". サッカーは大好きです is neutral; サッカーなら大好きです makes it clear that other sports, not so much. Don't swap one for the other without thinking about the meaning.

English uses "if" for everything, but Japanese doesn't. For "if X happens, (then) Y" (if it rains, if I get there early), the usual form is 〜たら, from lesson 17-2: 雨がふったら、行きません ✓. The なら of this lesson picks up a topic; it doesn't describe a sequence of events.
howToStudy: Tap 🔬 on example 1. 日曜日なら shows up as IF / WHEN and ひまですよ is the PREDICATE. Also notice ありますが, marked …BUT: it closes the Saturday half before the contrast.
Invent 4 broad questions and answer each one out loud, picking out one item with なら: 日本料理は好きですか。— すしなら好きです。 Use the potential from lesson 13-1 in at least one answer: 英語なら話せます。
Play tour guide for your city: for 4 topics (food, a beach or a park, shopping, a sport), give a recommendation with なら: 〜なら、〜がいいですよ。

grammar.title: Frequency: 一週間に三回
grammar.explanation:
To say **how often** you do something, Japanese uses **[period] + に + [number of times]**. 一週間に三回 = "three times a week", literally "in one week, three times". Notice the order: English puts the period last ("three times **a week**"); Japanese puts it first.
• **Times**: number + **回** (かい). 一回 (**いっ**かい), 二回 (にかい), 三回 (さんかい), 四回 (よんかい), 五回 (ごかい), 六回 (**ろっ**かい), 七回 (ななかい), 八回 (**はっ**かい, also はちかい), 九回 (きゅうかい), 十回 (**じゅっ**かい). The question is **何回** (なんかい).
• **Periods**: 一日 (**いちにち**, "one day"), 一週間 (いっしゅうかん), 一か月 (いっかげつ), 一年 (いちねん).
• The same formula works for **how long** per period: 一日に一時間 = "one hour a day".
• **The number takes no particle**: 一週間に | 三回 | ジムに | 行きます. The frequency block usually comes at the start of the sentence or right before the verb.
• To answer roughly, use **ぐらい**: 三回ぐらい; 一時間ぐらい.
• In the sentence, 一週間に is **TIME** and 三回 is **QUANTITY**; the **PREDICATE** is still at the end. Read from the end: "goes" → where? → to the gym → how many times? → three → in what period? → in a week.
grammar.structure: [period] に [number] 回 … [verb] · [period] に 何回…？

examples.jp: ペドロさんは一週間に三回ジムに行きます。
examples.kana: ペドロさんはいっしゅうかんにさんかいジムにいきます。
examples.romaji: Pedoro-san wa isshūkan ni sankai jimu ni ikimasu.
examples.en: Pedro goes to the gym three times a week. [lit. in one week, three times]

examples.jp: 一日に何時間ぐらい日本語を勉強しますか。— 一日に一時間ぐらいです。
examples.kana: いちにちになんじかんぐらいにほんごをべんきょうしますか。— いちにちにいちじかんぐらいです。
examples.romaji: Ichinichi ni nanjikan gurai nihongo o benkyō shimasu ka. — Ichinichi ni ichijikan gurai desu.
examples.en: About how many hours a day do you study Japanese? — About one hour a day.

examples.jp: 一年に一回、家族に会いにブラジルに帰ります。
examples.kana: いちねんにいっかい、かぞくにあいにブラジルにかえります。
examples.romaji: Ichinen ni ikkai, kazoku ni ai ni Burajiru ni kaerimasu.
examples.en: Once a year, I go back to Brazil to see my family.

pitfalls: The order is period + に + times: 三回に一週間 ✗ → 一週間に三回 ✓. Don't copy the English order ("three times a week").
The "a" of "a week" (per week) is に, not の: 一週間の三回 ✗ → 一週間に三回 ✓.
No particle after the number: 三回をジムに行きます ✗ → 三回ジムに行きます ✓.
Watch the readings: 一回 is いっかい (いちかい ✗); 一日 meaning "one day" is いちにち. ついたち is a different word, "the first" of the month: 一日に三回 = いちにちにさんかい ✓.
howToStudy: Count aloud from 一回 to 十回 and mark in your notebook the readings that change: いっかい, ろっかい, はっかい, じゅっかい.
Tap 🔬 on example 1. 一週間に shows up as TIME, 三回 as QUANTITY (no particle) and ジムに as DESTINATION. The PREDICATE is 行きます: read it backwards.
Say 5 true sentences about your routine, each with a frequency: how often you work out, study, play Wagotabi, call someone. Use at least one with 一か月に and one with 一日に〜時間.

homework.intro: Do it by hand in your notebook. Write the kanji you already know and the rest in kana. Only then open the answer key, item by item. Circle what you got wrong and redo it the next day. If you have the Genki II Workbook, do this lesson's exercises too.

tasks.prompt: Rewrite with 〜てみる, in the form given. First make the て-form; then conjugate みる.

items.q: 食べる → "I want to try it"
着る → "May I try it on?"

a.jp: 着てみてもいいですか
a.kana: きてみてもいいですか
a.romaji: kite mite mo ii desu ka

items.note: 〜てもいいですか (lesson 06-3) after みる.
行く has an irregular て-form: 行って.

a.kana: つかってみてください

items.q: 運転する → "I want to try it"

a.kana: うんてんしてみたいです

items.note: む → んで; then みる → みましょう.

tasks.prompt: Answer using the word in parentheses + なら. In the contrasts, use は for the part that doesn't work.

items.q: 日本料理は好きですか。（すし）
items.note: From the group (Japanese food) to one item (sushi).
The potential from lesson 13-1: 会う → 会える.

items.q: おいしいパンが買いたいんですが。（パン → 駅の近くの店がいい）

a.jp: パンなら、駅の近くの店がいいですよ。
a.kana: パンなら、えきのちかくのみせがいいですよ。
a.romaji: Pan nara, eki no chikaku no mise ga ii desu yo.

items.note: Use 1: a recommendation about the topic the other person brought up.

items.q: 月曜日にパーティーに来られますか。（月曜日はだめ／金曜日なら行ける）

a.jp: 月曜日はちょっと…。金曜日なら行けます。
a.kana: げつようびはちょっと…。きんようびならいけます。
a.romaji: Getsuyōbi wa chotto…. Kin'yōbi nara ikemasu.

items.note: Contrast: は + ちょっと… for the day that doesn't work, なら for the day that does.

items.q: ピアノがひけますか。（ピアノはだめ／ギターならひける）

a.jp: ピアノはひけませんが、ギターならひけます。
a.romaji: Piano wa hikemasen ga, gitā nara hikemasu.

items.note: ひく → ひける (potential), with は for the piano and なら for the guitar.

items.q: I go to the supermarket twice a week.

a.jp: 一週間に二回スーパーに行きます。
a.kana: いっしゅうかんににかいスーパーにいきます。
a.romaji: Isshūkan ni nikai sūpā ni ikimasu.

items.q: How many times a month do you call your family?

a.jp: 一か月に何回家族に電話しますか。
a.kana: いっかげつになんかいかぞくにでんわしますか。
a.romaji: Ikkagetsu ni nankai kazoku ni denwa shimasu ka.

items.note: 電話する takes に: 家族に電話する.

items.q: Take this medicine three times a day.

a.jp: このくすりは一日に三回飲んでください。
a.kana: このくすりはいちにちにさんかいのんでください。
a.romaji: Kono kusuri wa ichinichi ni sankai nonde kudasai.

items.note: In English you "take" medicine; in Japanese you "drink" it: くすりを飲む. Here 一日 is いちにち.

items.q: I sleep about six hours a day.

a.jp: 一日に六時間ぐらいねます。
a.kana: いちにちにろくじかんぐらいねます。

items.q: Someday I want to try wearing a kimono.

a.jp: いつか着物を着てみたいです。
a.kana: いつかきものをきてみたいです。
a.romaji: Itsuka kimono o kite mitai desu.

items.q: (A friend invites you to go out to a club. You're not into clubs, but you like karaoke.) If it's karaoke, I'll go!

a.jp: カラオケなら行きます！
a.kana: カラオケならいきます！

items.note: なら picks the option that works for you, after the topic (going out) has already come up.

tasks.prompt: A Japanese friend is going to visit your city and asks what to do there. Write 5 or 6 sentences: 2 recommendations with なら (food, a place…), 1 with 〜てみてください, 1 telling about something you tried with 〜てみました and 1 with a frequency (〜に〜回). Then read them aloud and record yourself on your phone.

items.q: Model (match its structure, not its words):

a.jp: ブラジル料理なら、フェイジョアーダを食べてみてください。とてもおいしいですよ。海なら、コパカバーナがいいです。わたしも一か月に二回ぐらい行きます。きょねん、そこではじめてサーフィンをしてみました。むずかしかったですが、とても楽しかったです。
a.kana: ブラジルりょうりなら、フェイジョアーダをたべてみてください。とてもおいしいですよ。うみなら、コパカバーナがいいです。わたしもいっかげつににかいぐらいいきます。きょねん、そこではじめてサーフィンをしてみました。むずかしかったですが、とてもたのしかったです。
a.romaji: Burajiru ryōri nara, feijoāda o tabete mite kudasai. Totemo oishii desu yo. Umi nara, Kopakabāna ga ii desu. Watashi mo ikkagetsu ni nikai gurai ikimasu. Kyonen, soko de hajimete sāfin o shite mimashita. Muzukashikatta desu ga, totemo tanoshikatta desu.
a.en: If it's Brazilian food, try the feijoada. It's really good. If it's the beach, Copacabana is good. I go there about twice a month, too. Last year I tried surfing there for the first time. It was hard, but it was a lot of fun.

items.note: Check: なら right after the noun, without だ; 〜てみる with the correct て-form; and the frequency as [period]に[number]回, with no particle after the number.

practice.what: Play in an N4-level area, if you have reached one. Hunt the dialogues for 〜てみる (〜てみて, 〜てみたい, 〜てみる) and なら. For each なら, say out loud which topic it picked up. Log the session in Immersion → Games and paste one of those lines into 🔬 Anatomy.
Drills → Conjugation: warm up the て-form, the base of 〜てみる. Then Drills → 🔬 Anatomy → 🧱 Build from the end with example 3 of point c, starting from 帰ります.

Whenever you find a sentence with なら, 〜てみる or a frequency (〜に〜回) in the game, in a video or on a website, save it in sentence Mining, with its translation. The goal is to collect 5 before you move on to Lesson 14.
Tap 🔊 on each example in this lesson and repeat along 3 times. In 一週間, the っ takes a full beat: い・っ・しゅ・う・か・ん is 6 beats. The same in いっかい: い・っ・か・い.
Record your tips for your city (homework h4) in 45 seconds or less. Listen and check that each なら came after a topic and that the numbers with 回 came out with the right reading.

culture.title: やたい: festival food stalls
culture.body: At **まつり** and summer fireworks festivals, the streets near the temple or shrine usually fill up with **やたい**: food stalls set up for the event. The classics are たこやき, やきそば (noodles stir-fried on a griddle), やきとり, かきごおり (shaved ice with syrup), わたあめ (cotton candy) and りんごあめ (candy apples). Many stalls also offer games, such as きんぎょすくい, where you try to scoop up goldfish with a small paper net. In general, eating while walking down the street is not considered very polite in Japan, but at festivals it is normal to eat standing near the stalls, and payment is usually in cash. In Fukuoka, some やたい open at night all year round and are famous for their ramen.
culture.try: Pick 3 やたい foods and say out loud: 〜を食べてみたいです。 Then answer a frequency question: 一年に何回おまつりに行きますか。 Finally, imagine a friend says あまいものが食べたい。 and answer with なら: あまいものなら、わたあめがいいですよ。

checklist: I can make 〜てみる with any verb, from the て-form, without looking: 食べてみる, 行ってみる, してみる.
I use 〜てみたいです, 〜てみました, 〜てみてください and 〜てみてもいいですか in real situations (a shop, a restaurant, a trip).
I know the difference between 食べてみました (I tried it) and 食べたことがあります (I have eaten it before).
I can respond to a topic with noun + なら, without だ, to recommend something or to make a contrast: 日曜日ならひまです。
I can say and ask about frequency with [period]に[number]回: 一週間に三回, 一日に何時間…？
I read 一回, 六回, 八回, 十回 and 一日 (いちにち) correctly.
I did the homework, checked it against the answer key and redid what I got wrong.
If I have the Genki II Workbook: I did this lesson's exercises on 〜てみる, なら and frequency.
